entities.summary:
Basilides (b. 117 CE, Alexandria) was a monarch or head of state of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Alexandria.

He played a key role in the development of early Christianity, serving as the bishop of Alexandria and a prominent figure in the Christological debates of the 2nd century CE.

Basilides' teachings emphasized the importance of spiritual enlightenment and the attainment of gnosis, a state of direct spiritual knowledge, which differed from the more dogmatic and liturgical approaches of other early Christian leaders.

Despite his influence, Basilides' ideas were largely lost to history until the 19th century, when they were rediscovered by scholars and reevaluated in the context of early Christian theology.

Basilides' legacy continues to be felt in the development of Christian mysticism and the study of early Christian theology, with many scholars regarding him as a pivotal figure in the evolution of Christian thought.

"The soul is the heaven of heaven, and the heaven of heaven is the soul." - Basilides
